items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: I was with Fletcher... I walked in Doc Hyder's band... Fletcher started giving me all the first parts... I moved over. Now tonight we're working 155th Street there.

ctx.x: You know. So you had to keep pushing, pushing, pushing, pushing, just do the best you could do. So I said all right, thank you very much. And you keep plugging, keep plugging, but one day somebody will call you.

So I was -- as I say, I got into New York. I was walking Seventh Avenue. I ran into a guy, he say -- what are you doing? I'm here, well I'm looking for a job. Okay. I knew him. I met him in Washington, D. C. He said 'well, Fletcher Henderson is looking for a trumpet player.' I said, 'he is?' Yeah. I said, 'where does he live?' He give me the address. Says 'they're in there rehearsing now.'

So I went up to Fletcher's house, knocked on the door, you know. I said my name is Herman Autrey. I was sent here. I heard…

items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: I went with Fletcher Henderson job in his house and took over the job as playing first trumpet

ctx.x: What happened to you the first time you went to the Rhythm Club?

Well, when I -- (laughs) God damn! Thank God I was blowing. I was playing, but I never hung up on this thing like Sedric. I never had that, because well that happened downtown where I told you Pops Foster went in for me, stood up for me, and I went and played and everybody liked me, and I was a good guy. When I came uptown, and I went on -- another thing I was blowing, but I never really had to stretch until I went with Fletcher Henderson job in his house and took over the job as playing first trumpet, and he…
That's why -- that was it, you know. That was my, you know, one of those things. I happened to have what was needed, and I kept going, and kept moving, you know.
